brief: Goldman's Capital Solutions Group head Miriam Wheeler says non-investment-grade issuance for AI data centers has stopped: zero new deals in the month since late September, versus roughly 30 deals over the prior year, often one every one to two weeks over the summer. Spreads reflect the shift: AI high-yield paper has widened to about 425bp versus 265bp for non-AI BB/B, and AI investment-grade spreads have widened to 140bp, 40bp over non-AI IG. The retreat reflects project-completion risk: investment-grade tenant wraps activate only once a facility is built, developers get a 180-day grace period before a tenant can terminate, and only 468MW of about 4GW financed by tracked bonds has been delivered, leaving Texas's possible moratorium and a legislature not adjourning until May 2027 as live risks. Chips are roughly 75% of facility cost versus 25% for shell and power, and 15-20 year leases sit behind bonds that mature in five, a mismatch Goldman also flags for neoclouds. CoreWeave, the largest tenant, says it will skip unsecured debt for an investment-grade delayed-draw loan instead. Wheeler sees bifurcation, not systemic contagion, and argues shrinking supply raises the value of what already exists.
